sections.title: CERT Top Module Architecture (MMT & Lifter)
learningObjectives: Understand why CERT top modules (MMT and Lifter) require dedicated integration engineering
Recognize how this builds on payload fundamentals from L2-M2
sections.content: Of the confirmed payload configurations introduced in L2-M2, DiFacto's CERT top modules - specifically the Material Movement Trolley (MMT) and Lifter modules - introduce active mechanical actuation on top of the mobile base. This module provides the advanced integration training these top modules require, beyond general operator payload awareness.

keyTerms.note: DiFacto's confirmed active payload interfaces, including MMT (Material Movement Trolley) and Lifter modules.

sections.title: Mechanics of MMT & Lifter Stability
learningObjectives: Understand the mechanical stability factors of MMT and Lifter actuation
Recognize how load height and trolley engagement alter center of gravity
sections.content: CERT Lifter and MMT configurations must manage load stability as vertical lift height changes or as heavy trolleys engage and disengage. This compounds the center-of-gravity considerations introduced in L2-M2's safety coverage. A unit's stability profile shifts whenever lift height changes or an MMT latch transfers load weight.

keyTerms.note: The point where a load's weight is balanced; it shifts during Lifter elevation and MMT trolley transfers.

video.title: CERT top module stability in 30 seconds
video.transcript: CERT top module stability, in 30 seconds. Active top modules like MMT and Lifter change how weight sits on the robot. As a Lifter raises or an MMT latches a trolley, the center of gravity shifts. Account for load height, latch state, and deceleration limits together.

sections.title: Configuring MMT & Lifter Parameters
learningObjectives: Understand the key parameters involved in configuring CERT top modules
Recognize the relationship between configuration limits and load-specific requirements
sections.content: Configuration parameters for CERT top modules typically include Lifter stroke height limits, speed and acceleration caps when raised, and MMT latch-confirmation timeouts, all calibrated to the specific load being handled. Follow DiFacto's payload technical documentation for the exact configuration workflow and safe operating ranges for each CERT module.

sections.title: Safety Clearances for Active Top Modules
learningObjectives: Understand safety considerations unique to MMT and Lifter actuation
Recognize how this extends the general loaded-payload safety principles from L2-M2
sections.content: Beyond the general loaded-payload safety principles covered in L2-M2, MMT and Lifter configurations require additional vertical and dock-entry clearance checks. Overhanging trolleys or raised lift platforms can extend beyond the base robot footprint and alter sensor visibility. Cell and workspace design must account for the full actuated envelope, not just the unloaded base footprint.

keyTerms.note: The full 3D space occupied by the robot and its CERT top module across all lift heights and trolley states.

sections.title: Integration With Fixed Equipment
learningObjectives: Understand how MMT and Lifter modules coordinate with fixed stations
Recognize handshake timing and latch-verification requirements
sections.content: MMT docking and Lifter transfers require precise positioning and confirmed mechanical engagement at fixed stations. Handshake timing from L3B-M4 must wait for verified limit-switch or sensor confirmation that lift positioning or MMT latching is complete before signaling ready. Otherwise you risk a premature signal exchange or a dropped transfer.

sections.title: Testing and Validating CERT Top Modules
learningObjectives: Apply testing principles specifically to MMT and Lifter integration
Know that validation must cover the full range of payload weights and lift positions
sections.content: Validation for CERT top modules should test across the full operational envelope - from empty to maximum rated payload, across all required Lifter heights and MMT docking stations - not just a single unloaded test pass. Confirm mechanical stability, latch sensing, and handshake timing hold up consistently.

keyTerms.note: The complete range of payload weights, lift heights, and docking conditions the application will use.

questions.question: Why do CERT top modules (MMT and Lifter) require dedicated integration engineering?
options: They are the only modules that ever use Fleet Manager
They add active mechanical actuation and shifting load profiles on top of the mobile base
They carry heavier loads than the mobile base is rated for
questions.feedback: Correct. Active top modules introduce vertical actuation, latching, and shifting load stability.

questions.question: How do Lifter elevation and MMT trolley transfers affect load stability?
options: Stability depends only on floor smoothness, not lift height
Stability is fixed once the robot leaves the dock
Stability shifts as lift height changes or a trolley latches and transfers weight
questions.feedback: Correct. Lift height and trolley engagement alter the center of gravity during operation.

questions.question: What clearance consideration is specific to MMT and Lifter configurations?
options: The full actuated envelope, including overhanging trolleys and raised lift heights
Only the floor-level clearance beneath the unloaded base
questions.feedback: Correct. Workspace design must account for the full actuated envelope, not just the unloaded base footprint.

questions.question: A Lifter handshake reuses a fixed short delay instead of waiting for verified position confirmation. What risk does the lesson name?
options: A premature signal exchange before lifting or latching is actually complete
A longer cycle because signals arrive too late
questions.feedback: Correct. Handshakes must wait for verified confirmation that lift positioning or MMT latching is complete.

questions.question: What should validation testing cover for a CERT top module integration?
options: Only the lowest lift height at one station
The full operational envelope across rated payload weights, lift heights, and docking stations
questions.feedback: Correct. Full operational envelope testing ensures stability, sensing, and handshake timing hold up across real conditions.
